We believe that this change in deformation modes at 20 K, promoted by low stacking-fault energies, is primarily responsible for the groundbreaking fracture toughness.

We believe that these alloys develop fracture resistance through a progressive synergy of deformation mechanisms, dislocation glide, stacking-fault formation, nanotwinning, and phase transformation, which act in concert to prolong strain hardening that simultaneously elevates strength and ductility, leading to exceptional toughness.
